doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Lou Rawls band, Alias and Jaco
title: Joining Lou Rawls and playing daily with Don Alias
summary: Rowe recalls Montalbano's excitement at joining Lou Rawls. He says the best part was making music every day with percussionist Don Alias, with Jaco Pastorius briefly in the band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: So let me ask about a few people that you’ve shared the bandstand with. I remember when you left to go play with Lou Rawls, and I think you were pretty excited about that.
I remember going to your house and I think you had a Rhodes —
And you were working on the music and you know, I felt really happy for you. Was that a good experience? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

That was a great experience. That was a wonderful experience, especially becoming friends with some of the people in the band — Don Alias in particular. So I highly recommend, of course our friend is gone now, but the idea of going on the road with Don Alias, more so actually than Lou Rawls, it was thrilling to me. And every day was a thrill really, because we played every day. He and I played every day. Virtually every day, aside from travel days.
You mean the two of you?
Okay. You’d find a way to —

We’d find a way to — we’d get up early, have some coffee and go right to the club and, you know the lights would be off and the club would be shut down and we’d come in through the kitchen and we’d play. Whether it was with organ and drums or electric piano and a set of bongos, or whatever it was, or two keyboards, or anything. We made music every day. Maybe that was the single most inspiring time of my life, or inspired maybe I should say — with Don. And of course then Jaco [Pastorius] was on the scene then, before anybody knew who he was. He did actually play in the band for a minute. He didn’t last long.
